title: Asteria Labs - post-launch stability and budget retune
summary: Quick check-in after their public launch: usage spiked, a subset of routes showing higher p95 latency, FinOps wants immediate cost levers. Discussed batching/kv cache settings, fallback models, and private routing for sensitive requests. Agreed to run a 24h synthetic load and provide per-route cost breakdown + security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, um we wanted to do a short post-launch check in and make sure the performance/cost story is working for you.
[00:08] Ravi Patel: Yeah thanks Maya, busy week. Usage basically doubled the first 48 hours after launch, which is great but we've seen, uh, some tail latency spikes on the /generate-order-summary route.
[00:18] Sofia Gomez: For us the main thing is those p95s — usually fine but during the morning batch we saw 2 to 3 second jumps, and it's impacting the frontend.
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: thanks for the detail Sofia, quick clarifying q; are those requests using the long context model or the 8k?
[00:35] Liam Brooks: It's mixed — product set them to the 32k fallback because of some edge cases but most traffic is 8k.
[00:41] Diego Alvarez: OK — that matters because the KV cache and attention kernel hit rate differs. We also, um, noticed that a small percent of requests are getting routed to the larger variant during autoscale bursts which increases latency.
[00:53] Anya Li: From FinOps perspective the cost bump is visible — tokens and the larger model route both contributing. Can we temporarily route to quantized variant for non-sensitive traffic?
[01:03] Maya Chen: Yes that's an option — we can enable a canary route that prefers the quantized 8-bit variant for 70% of traffic, and keep the full-precision as fallback for failures or high-quality flagged requests.
[01:12] Tom O'Neal: Security question: if we use quantized models or caching, does any PII leave our VPC? We need to keep logs out of hosted storage — KMS keys only.
[01:22] Priya Nair: good call Tom — we can do Private routing for those flagged endpoints, which keeps the inference plane in your VPC and honors customer KMS. For hosted routes we keep audit logs and retention policies per your compliance settings.
[01:32] Ravi Patel: How quickly can we toggle the routing policy? If the burst recurs in a couple hours we need the ability to flip back to the larger model for accuracy-sensitive runs.
[01:40] Diego Alvarez: Policies are immediate; toggles are API driven. We can also set automatic fallback: if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds, traffic moves to the full-precision model. That gives a safety net.
[01:50] Sofia Gomez: Could the KV cache be tuned? We suspect miss rates are high because of variable prefixes in the prompt.
[01:58] Diego Alvarez: Yes — prefix normalization helps. Also bumping the KV cache warmup TTL during expected bursts reduces cold starts. We'll share recommended config and an nginx-like caching shim for prompts.
[02:09] Anya Li: On the cost side, can you share per-route token and per-request cost breakdown? We need it for exec.
[02:16] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll send a per-route breakdown, and propose a simple throttling policy for non-critical background jobs.
[02:23] Liam Brooks: There's also a question on model eval drift — we saw slight quality deltas when quantized model answered complex multi-turn. What do you recommend for eval guardrails?
[02:33] Diego Alvarez: We'll set up a small eval harness with your prompt set; we can run A/B and flag regressions in Rouge/semantic similarity metrics. If the quantized variant dips beyond the agreed threshold we stop the canary.
[02:45] Ravi Patel: Perfect. Also legal asked for SOC 2 attestation and an export of audit logs for the pilot window.
[02:52] Tom O'Neal: Also need details on key rotation cadence and HSM support.
[02:55] Priya Nair: We'll share the SOC 2 report link and a step-by-step on how audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM. HSM/KMS integration is supported — we'll include the HSM diagrams.
[03:05] Anya Li: Any immediate quick wins you recommend?
[03:08] Diego Alvarez: Short term: enable quantized canary for 60-70% of non-sensitive traffic, increase KV cache TTL during morning peak, and add a soft throttle on background jobs. Medium term: run synthetic 24h load to validate autoscale and warm caches, and consider Dedicated pool if sustained throughput remains high.
[03:25] Liam Brooks: Dedicated pool — cost/benefit?
[03:27] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale, but there's a commitment. We'll model the tradeoffs and show the break-even point for your traffic shape.
[03:36] Ravi Patel: Alright, so next immediate actions — we want the per-route cost, the SOC2 and HSM docs, config changes to KV cache, and a proposal for a 24h synthetic run.
[03:45] Maya Chen: Great, we'll do that. Any other blockers?
[03:48] Sofia Gomez: One small thing: can we get a short runbook for troubleshooting when p95 blips happen? Likes steps, logs to check.
[03:56] Diego Alvarez: Yep we'll provide a triage checklist: check route, check KV miss rate, check GPU queue length, fallbacks, and telemetry links to trace.
[04:05] Ravi Patel: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[04:08] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with materials and propose times for the synthetic load window.
[04:12] [call ends ar 04:12]
